AUTHOR: Liu, MX; Wu, YJ; Li, RX; Lin, C
TITLE: LFN-YOLO: precision underwater small object detection via a lightweight reparameterized approach
SPECIES: Brackish: fish, small fish, crab, starfish, shrimp, jellyfish (URPC/TrashCan non-fish)
DATA: Brackish (11,205 images; fish results), URPC 2021 (7,543, invertebrates), TrashCan (7,212, debris); qualitative fish-tank deployment
V_EV: Sec 4.1: Brackish 'presence of numerous suspended particles in the water results in image blurring, reduced contrast, and even scattering artifacts'
D_EV: Sec 4.1: 'The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and testing sets in an 8:1:1 ratio.'
R_EV: Sec 5.3: 'we trained both the LFN-YOLO and YOLOv8n models using the Brackish dataset' then deployed in 'a 200L fish tank' with fish fry; results shown qualitatively (Figs 10-11)
E_EV: Sec 5/Table 3: only 'precision, recall, mAP@0.5' and model size/FLOPs reported
ARCH: LFN-YOLO (YOLOv8n-based with RepGhost, SPD-Conv, GFPN neck, CLLAHead, DFL)
METR: P, R, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, params, GFLOPs, FPS
NOTE: Only Brackish contains fish (field fixed camera, allowed dataset); URPC and TrashCan are benchmark/non-fish. Brackish randomly re-split 8:1:1 at image level (original predefined split is frame-based). External test only qualitative: Brackish-trained model run on fish fry in a 200 L tank (Figs 10-11) -> R1=Y, R3=N. IoU threshold 0.5 for mAP is not a confidence threshold.
